The Stoney Lake example study, as read

Source: R/data.R
detqc_example.Rd

Four walleye tracked by 20 receivers from 2 to 10 June 2024 in Stoney Lake, Ontario, read from the files stoney_detections.csv, stoney_receivers.csv and stoney_tag_specs.csv in system.file("extdata", package = "detqc") with read_detections(), read_deployments() and read_animals(). The study is simulated from known tracks with the range and movement models of the positionR packages; no real data are included with the package. ST-02 and ST-03 carry depth sensors, whose readings are raw counts here. ST-02 dies at 02:00 UTC on 4 June 2024, and its tag is then heard only at station S011. example_mortality is the same study prepared for the mortality rules.

Usage

detqc_example

Format

A list of three data frames:

detections

3,297 detections: datetime (UTC), receiver_serial, transmitter, animal_id, station_id, sensor_raw, sensor_value and sensor_unit.

deployments

20 deployments of 20 receivers at 20 stations, with the contract's deployment columns.

animals

4 transmitters on 4 animals, with release time and place, tag model, serial and life, transmission delays and, for ST-02 and ST-03, the depth calibration.

Source

Simulated by https://github.com/jakebrownscombe/detqc/blob/main/data-raw/stoney_example.R and read by https://github.com/jakebrownscombe/detqc/blob/main/data-raw/detqc_example.R. Both scripts are in the repository and not in the installed package.

Examples

# Rows in each table, and detections per animal
sapply(detqc_example, nrow)
#>  detections deployments     animals 
#>        3297          20           4 
table(detqc_example$detections$animal_id)
#> 
#> ST-01 ST-02 ST-03 ST-04 
#>   846  1273   463   715
